draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Kovalam! This fishing village on the East Coast Road was known to Europeans as Covelong, and in 1719 a Frenchman got permission from the Nawab of the Carnatic to set up a trading post here. Today it's all about the beach, the fishing boats and surfing.
draft.hungryLine: This is a fishing village, so ask around for whatever fresh catch the boats brought in today.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Malik ibn Dinar Mosque is a 4 min walk, and Fisherman's Cove, built on the ruins of an 18th-century Belgian castle, is about 18 minutes away.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Head down to the beach and watch the fishing boats and surfers, it's what Covelong is known for today.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Covelong was one of the early Asian trading posts of the Ostend Company, a trading company from what is now Belgium.

spots.name: Malik ibn Dinar Mosque

spots.name: Taj Fisherman's Cove Resort & Spa
spots.detail: 18 min walk · Beach resort on the ramparts of a ruined Belgian castle

tips.title: Respect the mosque.
tips.body: The Malik ibn Dinar Mosque holds a saint's grave, so dress modestly and be quiet when you visit.

tips.title: Try a surf session.
tips.body: Covelong is known for surfing, so it's a good place to get on a board.

story.title: Cabelon
story.body: Covelong grew up as a trading settlement in the early 18th century. Europeans knew it as Cabelon.

story.title: A trading post
story.body: In 1719 Godefroy de la Merveille got permission from Sa'adatullah Khan I, Nawab of the Carnatic, to set up a trading post here.

story.title: The Ostend Company
story.body: The settlement became linked with the Ostend Company, which made it one of its early Asian trading posts. A castle went up, and its ruined ramparts now carry the Fisherman's Cove resort.

story.title: Beach and surf
story.body: Kovalam is now a fishing village about 40 km south of central Chennai. It's known for its beach, its fishing community and surfing.
